archetype.name: Pocket Passer (late-career, underneath)
archetype.definition: A 43-year-old who barely runs and wins with timing and accuracy into the short middle of the field, while the arm that once drove the deep game now misses more than it hits.

report.headline: Volume keeps him relevant; underneath precision can't offset sacks and missed deep shots.
report.take:
Rodgers in 2026 is a volume passer on a below-average efficiency line. His 224.1 passing yards a game rank 18th of 55, but his -0.056 EPA per dropback ranks 33rd and trails the league's qualifier average of -0.027, and his 6.21 yards per attempt ranks 36th. None of that is new. His EPA per play ranked 27th in 2024 and 30th in 2025, so this is who he has been for three seasons: a competent distributor, not the 2020-21 version who led the league. McCarthy keeps putting the ball in his hands anyway. Pittsburgh's pass rate over expected ranks 4th even though its rushing EPA ranks 1st and its passing EPA ranks 25th.

The offense works when the ball goes short and to the middle. On throws of 0-9 air yards he completes 72% with a +4.4 CPOE and 9 touchdowns, and throws over the middle return 0.347 EPA a play, the only direction that adds value. His tight ends carry the passing game on a per-play basis: Freiermuth produces 0.297 EPA per target and Washington 0.194, while DK Metcalf, who leads the team with 74 targets, gets only 0.031. Two parts of the menu drain value. The 87 throws behind the line (screens and swing passes) cost 0.123 EPA a play. And the deep ball has gone cold: 21.2% completions, a -13.2 CPOE and a 23.1% success rate on 52 attempts. His aggressiveness rose to 17.17% from 14.5% last year, so he is taking more tight-window chances, and they aren't landing.

The raw numbers hide where the damage comes from: sacks in key spots. He is pressured on only 19.4% of dropbacks, 14th-lowest of 45, yet 34.7% of those pressures become sacks, which ranks 32nd. That rate was 0.341 last year and 0.315 in 2024, so it is a long-running trait of a statuesque passer who waits for the play to come open, not a line problem. Third down is where it bites hardest. He has been sacked 19 times there (of 31 overall), posts -0.215 EPA a play and converts 30.1% facing an average of 7.6 yards to go. The red zone is similar: 10 touchdowns, but -0.189 EPA and 7 sacks. The genuine positive is ball security. His 1.7% interception rate sits below the league's 2.5%, and his bad-throw rate fell 2.4 points from last season.

The direction is not encouraging. Over the last three games his yards per attempt slid to 5.53, his CPOE to -5, and his yardage to 180.7 a game, 43.4 below his season average, while the team went 1-2. Starting guard Mason McCormick (93% of snaps) is now on IR with an estimated return in January, which weakens interior protection for a quarterback who already converts pressure into sacks at a high rate. Michael Pittman's expected return adds a reliable target. Still, the most likely path is a ~200-yard passer whose touchdown rate cools and whose value depends on game script.

strengths.title: Accuracy into the short middle
strengths.body: His timing and placement on short throws are still above expectation, with a positive CPOE under 10 air yards and his best EPA by far over the middle. This is a skill that holds up as arm strength fades. It is the backbone of the offense and should last.

strengths.title: Tight ends drive the efficiency
strengths.body: Freiermuth and Washington are his most productive targets per play by a wide margin, which fits a passer who works the seams and short middle. It is repeatable because it comes from scheme and the route tree, not from a few big plays. It also gives the offense a clear answer against defenses that are soft on tight ends.

strengths.title: He doesn't give the ball away
strengths.body: His interception rate is nearly a point under the league average, and his bad-throw rate improved from last season. Veteran processing keeps the costly mistakes rare. Three of his six interceptions came on deep shots, so the risk sits where his aggressiveness rose.

concerns.title: Pressure turns into sacks
concerns.body: He is rarely pressured, but a third of those pressures end in sacks, and most of his sacks come on third down, where his EPA collapses. His career shows the same pressure-to-sack rate for years, so this is his style at 43, not bad luck. With a starting guard on IR, expect it to persist or worsen.

concerns.title: Deep ball no longer lands
concerns.body: A 21.2% completion rate and a -13.2 CPOE on throws of 20+ yards mean most shots are wasted plays. A few touchdowns keep the EPA slightly positive. He is throwing into tighter windows more often than last year, and the arm and accuracy that once made that pay are not there.

concerns.title: Efficiency sliding since midseason
concerns.body: His yards per attempt and accuracy have both dropped over the last three games, along with his yardage. The dip spans easy and hard defenses alike, and it lines up with the line getting thinner, so it doesn't look like a schedule blip.

trend.note: He peaked in Weeks 3-5 with three straight three-touchdown games and has not topped 253 yards since. The last three games averaged 180.7 yards on a 5.53 YPA, although his EPA per dropback held roughly level thanks to fewer turnovers.

nextGame.headline: Denver's pressure, a Friday turnaround and wind stack against him.
nextGame.body:
Denver attacks his two weak spots. Its defensive hit rate ranks 2nd and its explosive-pass rate allowed ranks 5th, so expect quick contact on a passer who turns pressure into sacks and few big plays downfield. The openings are underneath and on the ground. Denver allows 271.7 passing yards a game to quarterbacks (27th), gives up 0.44 EPA per play to opposing top tight ends (28th), and sees a larger share of targets go to tight ends than the league norm. Its run defense ranks 23rd in EPA against Pittsburgh's top-ranked rushing attack. As a 3-point home underdog with a 38.5 total and an early forecast of 17 mph wind with gusts to 39 (hedged, since it is 81 hours out), the smart script is run-heavy with short tight-end throws, which caps his ceiling.

On his side, McCarthy is "very confident" Michael Pittman (78% of snaps in his three games) returns from the foot injury. That would give Rodgers a third reliable receiver ahead of Germie Bernard, whose targets have cost EPA. The interior line remains the worry: Mason McCormick is on IR into January, and Gennings Dunker has only been designated to return. For Denver, starting safety Brandon Jones (91% of snaps) sat last week with a hamstring injury. If he misses this one too, the middle of the field where Rodgers does his best work gets softer.

keyMatchups.title: Denver's rush vs his sack habit
keyMatchups.body: Denver gets hits on quarterbacks at the league's second-highest rate. Rodgers converts pressure into sacks at a bottom-tier rate. Third-and-long drives are where this game swings.

keyMatchups.title: Tight ends against a soft spot
keyMatchups.body: Denver ranks near the bottom against top tight ends and sees more tight-end targets than average. That plays straight into Freiermuth's per-target efficiency, the most reliable route to yards in this game.

keyMatchups.title: Wind and the run game
keyMatchups.body: If the gusty forecast holds, the deep game he already struggles with mostly disappears. Pittsburgh's elite rushing EPA against a below-average Denver run defense becomes the logical plan, which lowers his passing volume.

nextGame.watch: Whether McCarthy leans on the league's top-ranked run game in the wind, or keeps asking Rodgers to throw on third-and-long into Denver's pass rush.

restOfSeason.body:
Expect what the three-year sample says he is: a mid-pack efficiency passer with good touch underneath, real volume because of play-calling, and a sack problem that is part of his style. The short-middle accuracy and low interception rate are sustainable, since both have held through the slide. The early-season touchdown bursts are less so. They leaned on deep scores at a low completion rate and a red zone that produces touchdowns despite negative EPA. Losing McCormick hurts a quarterback who doesn't escape pressure, and late-season weather in Pittsburgh threatens the deep game further.

Pittman's return and a tight-end-friendly approach should keep him in the 190-230 yard range most weeks, with about one touchdown a game being the honest midpoint. His weekly value will track game script. Trailing games pile up attempts, while a lead or bad weather hands the ball to a top rushing offense.
swingFactors: Interior line health with McCormick out and Dunker's return
Pittman's return and whether it diverts targets from Metcalf
McCarthy's run/pass balance and late-season weather

confidence.note: Ten starts and a stable three-year profile, but recent decline and line injuries add uncertainty.
